note: Triennial election of Tyrone County Council, polled Wednesday 1 June 1927. Nominations were taken on Wednesday 20 April 1927, and the Derry Journal of 22 April 1927 prints the full county list division by division under 'Tyrone County and Rural Elections: List of Nominations'. It says 'Only three contests are threatened for the County Council' — Fintona, Aughnacloy and Carrickmore — but the result reports of 2 and 3 June record only two polls, so the Carrickmore challenger withdrew. Killeter is given in the article's text rather than the list, where no nomination was made and Mr. Robert Thompson continued. That makes twenty-six divisions. Dungannon does not appear in the 1927 list because, as in 1924, the urban divisions were nominated locally; its member, Joseph Newell, J.P., was returned unopposed (Belfast Telegraph, 21 April 1927, p. 10). The polled divisions keep the recorded results of 1 June, with the nomination notice added as a second citation. One discrepancy is left on the record: the Belfast Telegraph of 2 June 1927 gives the new council as 25 Unionists and 10 Nationalists — thirty-five members — which is more than the twenty-six divisions printed here, while the Irish News of 10 June 1930 gives twenty-four. The council's total membership is therefore not settled by the sources read, though every division printed is recorded. Johnston was the official Unionist candidate; M'Elroy stood for the Ratepayers' and Farmers' Association and was also defeated in the Seskinore division of Omagh Rural Council. The Ulster Herald of 4 June prints the total poll as 1,403 with 6 spoiled votes, but the votes sum to 1,402 and 1,402 + 6 = 1,408, so the poll and spoiled figures are left out. The division comprised Loughmuck, Fallaghearn, Ecclesville, Fintona, Seskinore and Dervaghroy, with six polling booths.
